cited_evidence: top_level_input.corpus contains n06-r01 with demand_score 9 and records n06-r01 through n06-r08 all have demand_score >= 3.
select_demand source selects records where demand_score >= 3 or fallback_ids, and selected/returned state artifacts have 8 rows.
normalize source sets allowed_record_ids = ['n06-r09', 'n06-r02', 'n06-r03', 'n06-r04', 'n06-r05', 'n06-r06', 'n06-r07', 'n06-r08'], excluding n06-r01.
normalize retained_df and needs_df state artifacts have 7 rows, and job_2 input needs contains only n06-r02 through n06-r08.
handoffs show exact hash handoff for needs from job_upstream_demand_provenance to job_downstream_coverage_priority, so downstream consumed the upstream-produced seven-row needs artifact.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution contains a fault in the upstream job. The top-level corpus has eight qualifying demand records because every record has demand_score >= 3, including n06-r01 with demand_score 9. select_demand retained eight rows, but normalize filtered the selected records through an allowed_record_ids list that omits n06-r01 and includes n06-r09 instead. This silently dropped the highest-demand stipulated record before the exact handoff to job_2. Job 2 then preserved and ranked the seven records it received, so the supported localization is upstream normalize.
